questions.question: Which combination is NOT a valid Java statement?
options: try with neither catch nor finally (no resources)
questions.explanation: A plain try block must be followed by at least one catch or a finally block.

questions.question: What does this print? try { System.out.print("A"); int n = Integer.parseInt("x"); System.out.print("B"); } catch (NumberFormatException e) { System.out.print("C"); } finally { System.out.print("D"); }
questions.explanation: The parse fails, so B is skipped. The catch prints C and finally prints D.

questions.question: Why does this not compile? try { cook(); } catch (Exception e) { } catch (NumberFormatException e) { }
options: The second catch is unreachable because Exception already catches it
A try can have only one catch block
catch blocks need a finally block after them
questions.explanation: Catch blocks must go from specific to general. Move the NumberFormatException block above the Exception block.

questions.question: What does this print? static int bill() { try { return 10; } finally { System.out.print("F "); } } and main does System.out.print(bill());
questions.explanation: The return value is computed, then finally runs and prints F, and only then does main print 10.

questions.question: What must a class implement to be used in a try-with-resources statement?
questions.explanation: Java calls close() automatically, which comes from AutoCloseable or its child Closeable.

questions.question: Why does this not compile? catch (java.io.IOException | Exception e) { }
options: The two types in a multi-catch cannot be parent and child
The variable must be named ex
Exception cannot be caught at all
questions.explanation: IOException is already a subclass of Exception, so the alternative is redundant and the compiler rejects it.

questions.question: Two resources r1 then r2 are opened in one try-with-resources, and each close() prints its name. The try body prints "use". What is printed?
questions.explanation: Resources are closed in the reverse order of opening, after the try body finishes.

questions.question: When an exception is thrown in a try block and no catch block matches, what happens?
options: The try block restarts from the top
finally runs, then the exception moves up to the caller
The program stops without running finally
questions.explanation: finally always gets its turn, and the unhandled exception then continues up the call stack.

questions.question: What is the problem here? static int count() { try { throw new RuntimeException("oven fault"); } finally { return 0; } }
options: It does not compile because of the return
The return in finally swallows the exception, so the fault is lost
RuntimeException must be declared with throws
questions.explanation: A return inside finally replaces any pending exception, so callers never learn about the oven fault.

questions.question: What is true about the variable e in a multi-catch such as catch (A | B e)?
options: It is implicitly final, so you cannot assign another exception to it
It lets you catch Error types as well
It makes the catch block run twice
It turns both exceptions into checked exceptions
questions.explanation: Java makes a multi-catch parameter implicitly final, so reassigning e inside the block does not compile.
